title: Polio couldn't stop him. He threw a world-record javelin anyway. October 22, 2026.
excerpt: From India's first spacecraft to reach the Moon, to a Science News CEO whose parents emigrated in 1960, to a railway network moving 135 million tonnes in a single month - October 22's five stories are about momentum that builds on itself.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is about something that kept going past the point it was expected to stop - a spacecraft that outlived its own mission timeline, a career built two generations removed from an immigrant arrival, a fellowship structured to keep someone coming back rather than visiting once, a freight network posting growth for a sixth straight month, and a leg weakened by polio that still produced a world-record throw.

October 22, 2008: India sent its first spacecraft to the Moon

ISRO launched Chandrayaan-1 aboard PSLV-C11 from Sriharikota, carrying 11 scientific instruments from six countries. Its Moon Impact Probe struck the lunar south pole, and the orbiter made over 3,400 orbits before contact was lost in August 2009 - groundwork for Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3's landing years later.

Her parents emigrated from India in 1960. In 2026, Forbes named her one of the world's top innovators at 59

Maya Ajmera, CEO of the Society for Science and publisher of Science News, was named to Forbes' 2026 '50 Over 50' Innovation list, having spent nearly two decades leading the Global Fund for Children before taking the helm of the century-old science publication.

A US statistics professor just won a fellowship to spend his summers teaching at IIT Bombay

Sujit Ghosh, a Professor of Statistics at NC State University, was awarded India's VAIBHAV Fellowship - chosen from 217 applicants worldwide - to spend one to two months a year for three years collaborating with IIT Bombay on statistics, biostatistics and climate science.

Indian Railways just moved 135 million tonnes of freight in a single month

Indian Railways loaded 135.35 million tonnes of freight in September 2026, up 6.14% year-on-year, with foodgrain loading up 25% and daily coal rake supply to power houses up 11.6% - part of six straight months of cumulative growth.

Polio couldn't stop him. He threw a world-record javelin anyway

Mahendra Gurjar, competing in the F42 classification due to a polio-related leg impairment, threw 61.17m at the Nottwil World Para Athletics Grand Prix in Switzerland in May 2025, breaking the previous world-record mark of 59.19m.

Five stories, one pattern: a spacecraft that kept orbiting past its planned life, a career that compounded two generations past an immigrant arrival, a fellowship built for return visits rather than a single trip, a freight network stacking up months of growth, and a body that kept performing past what polio was supposed to allow.
